newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Curve flattens again.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Curve flattens again.

text.p: The Australian bond yield curve flattened again on Tuesday as further steepening trades were unwound as the market took a cautious stance ahead of Wednesday's first quarter GDP.
The three/10-year bond futures had spiked to over 120 basis points last week after a weak retail trade report fuelled speculation of a further easing in monetary policy.

Although a further easing is seen possible this cycle, it is generally felt that such a move is not imminent given the Reserve Bank, which held its monthly board meeting today, only cut rates to 5.5 percent on May 23.
However, the market put in a mild outperformance against the U.S. during a low turnover session, which took the Australian/U.S. 10-year spread to around its lowest level in over three-years.

Spreads to Canada widened slightly after the result of the Canadian election, which will see the Liberal party form government again, although margins had narrowed when initial results suggested that they might lose power.
The New Zealand market firmed on a higher N.Z. TWI and as it played catch up to the rallies seen in the dollar bloc while it was on holiday on Monday.
